findings.claim: An audio object consists of object essence plus corresponding object properties.
The decoder interface pairs decoded object essence audio with timestamped updates for corresponding properties.
JOC reconstructs an ordered set of output objects and exposes one matrix domain per output object.
Object processing iterates declared output-object slots and matrix reconstruction emits those slots.
Presence and sequence side information controls decoding state, not authored cross-payload identity.
LFE is bypassed rather than processed by JOC.
OAMD retains object entries and defines bed, ISF, then dynamic ordering locally.
Metadata updates use shared frame/sample timing and sample offsets.
The companion timing description aligns metadata updates with PCM sample timing.
No clause equates JOC output count with OAMD count after any LFE offset.
No numeric permutation, skip, or identifier maps an OAMD entry to a JOC output slot.
Reset/splice handling initializes state but does not define persistent authored object identity.
The informative ADM guidance explains metadata timing and coordinate conversion, not a JOC PCM row identity map.
OAMD and JOC payloads share an EMDF configuration context and frame cadence.
The reviewed normative material does not state the required JOC-output-to-OAMD-object identity operation.

conclusion: Public semantics are partial: decoded JOC output is object essence and each domain preserves order, but the cross-domain object identity edge is unspecified.
